headline: Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia along with Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav jointly chair investor and strategic roundtables in Mumbai; Discussions focus on strengthening India’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) and unlocking investment opportunities
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia along with Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav jointly chair investor and strategic roundtables in Mumbai; Discussions focus on strengthening India’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) and unlocking investment opportunities

TMZ will strengthen India’s position on the global telecom manufacturing map: Union Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

⁠India's first-of-its-kind Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior will advance Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat

DoT and COAI Organise Investor Roundtable and Strategic Roundtable on Capitalising India’s Telecom Decade and Promoting Telecom Manufacturing Zone

04 AUG 2026 10:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India in collaboration with the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), organised two important industry engagements in Mumbai today to advance the proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) coming up in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. Both engagements were jointly chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region and Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh along with Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications. Both meetings mark a significant milestone in strengthening India's first-of-its-kind Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, which will advance Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector.

The first engagement was an Investor Roundtable focused on attracting investment and greater industry participation in the proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior. Leading telecom and electronics companies, including Qualcomm, NTT DATA, Jio and other leading companies participated in the investor roundtable. Discussions focused on the investment potential of the TMZ, strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities, promoting exports, reducing import dependence and creating a globally competitive telecom and electronics manufacturing ecosystem.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, said, “India must now transition from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. We must adopt a three-pronged strategy to achieve this transformation: increasing domestic value addition, creating intellectual property in India, and enabling Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured telecom products to reach every corner of the world.”

Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, said, “I would like to thank all the officials involved in this project. This important project is a joint step between Government of Madhya Pradesh and Union Government in the field of telecommunications. Madhya Pradesh has emerged as the top choice for set up industry especially related to manufacturing. With this in mind, I would like to invite you all to come and invest in Madhya Pradesh.”

Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, highlighted that “Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) is a unique and first of its kind facility that has been envisioned jointly by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and Union Ministry of Communications. TMZ will create deep value addition driven by Intellectual Property within India helping India becoming a part in global supply chain in line with Hon’ble Prime Minister’s Vision of Made in India for India and the World.”

In the first roundtable held in Delhi, investment commitments worth ₹3,500 crore and 14,000 job opportunities were assured by the industry for the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

At the conclusion of the Investor Roundtable at Mumbai, participating companies committed investments worth more than ₹2,000 crore, expected to generate above 4,000 employment opportunities under the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ). In total, a commitment of more than ₹5500 crores of investments and above 18,000 employment opportunities were given by the industry towards the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ).

Eight global tech leaders, including Qualcomm, Ericsson and Nokia, along with leading IT companies such as TCS and Tech Mahindra, have expressed interest in considering the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) as an investment destination and establishing global service support and development centres in the zone.

All three private telecom service providers—Bharti Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea—appreciated the initiative and leadership of the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia. They also affirmed that they would encourage their respective vendor ecosystems to explore opportunities for establishing supply chains and manufacturing facilities within the TMZ in Gwalior.

The second engagement was a Strategic Roundtable on “Capitalizing India’s Telecom Decade and Promoting Telecom Manufacturing Zone”. The strategic roundtable brought together key stakeholders from the telecom industry to deliberate on India’s next phase of telecom growth, strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and creating a globally competitive telecom ecosystem. Union Minister Sh. Jyotiraditya M. Scindia appreciated the role of investors in promoting Indian startup and Tech ecosystem. He invited the investors to India Mobile Congress being held from 7 to 10 October 2026 at Yashobhoomi New Delhi. The discussions also focused on identifying opportunities for greater industry participation and investment in the proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

The roundtable was held in continuation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July 2026 for establishment of India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior. The MoU envisages a 170 acres plug-and-play industrial cluster offering world-class infrastructure and an integrated ecosystem for telecom and electronics manufacturing, research and development, innovation and allied activities. At the Strategic Roundtable, the participating stakeholders deliberated on further opportunities for investment, manufacturing and employment in the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ).

The strategic roundtable reinforced the Government’s vision of moving India beyond being a telecom service provider towards becoming a global telecom product manufacturing and innovation hub. It also marked another important step towards translating the recently signed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) MoU into concrete investments, manufacturing and employment opportunities.

About Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior

The proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior is envisaged as an integrated 170-acre plug-and-play industrial cluster for telecom manufacturing, R&D and innovation, covering mobile devices, optical fibre, telecom equipment and next-generation 5G/6G technologies. Under the recently signed MoU, the Central Government is providing 100% funding support of ₹493 crore for Phase-I, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost along with various investor incentives.

The TMZ will be established through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) with 51% equity from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% from the Department of Telecommunications.

headline: Farmers voice strong support for Ethanol after meeting Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Farmers voice strong support for Ethanol after meeting Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

AIKCC leaders said during the meeting with Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh that Ethanol will increase farmers’ income and also secure the country’s energy

During the meeting with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, farmers said, “Ethanol is a new opportunity for farming”

“Farmers and the government should work together to break the wrong narrative on Ethanol”: AIKCC

“Not petrol, but Ethanol coming from the fields is the future of the country,” Farmer leaders from various states told Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Open discussion held on Ethanol and farmers’ income by farmer leaders from across the country at Krishi Bhavan, New Delhi

“The doors of Krishi Bhavan are open for farmers; farmers are like God”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

04 AUG 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi

A delegation of the All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC) met Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Tuesday and categorically stated that Ethanol is a big opportunity for the farming sector, provided its policy is farmer-centric and the correct price of the crop reaches the farmer directly. Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan carefully listened to all the suggestions of the farmer leaders and, while giving his guidance, assured that the Central Government will take the farmers’ views on Ethanol seriously. Shri Shivraj Singh said that farmers are like God for him and the doors of Krishi Bhavan are always open for farmers.

Farmer leaders from across the country speak openly on Ethanol at Krishi Bhavan

At Krishi Bhavan in New Delhi, a delegation of AIKCC met Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan. The delegation included farmer leaders from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and other parts of the country. The main focus of the meeting remained on Ethanol, farmers’ income, MSP (minimum support price), markets and the National Agriculture Policy. However, the farmers clearly said that they are in favour of Ethanol; they only want that the real benefit of this programme reaches the farmer and not only companies or middlemen.

What farmers said in favour of Ethanol

During the meeting, the farmer leaders made their stand on Ethanol clear and said that with Ethanol, the produce of the field will not remain limited only to the mandi (market), but will reach petrol pumps and the energy market. This will create a new and strong market for farmers. When Ethanol is made from sugarcane, maize, rice and other feedstocks, farmers will get more buyers and the problem of crop spoilage or storage will reduce.

The farmers said that they are not against Ethanol but are fully in its support. However, it is necessary that proper prices of any crop, whether maize or sugarcane, reach the farmers. The farmer representatives said that they want an Ethanol policy to create a new path for farming and not become a new worry for them. They said they are with Ethanol, if Ethanol also is with them.

‘It is necessary to clear misunderstandings on Ethanol’ – Farmer leaders

During the meeting, several farmer leaders said that confusion is being spread on social media and some platforms in the name of Ethanol – sometimes by saying that it damages vehicles, sometimes by saying that it harms farmers. The farmers demanded that the Union Agriculture Ministry and farmer organisations together clearly explain which crops will benefit in what way from Ethanol and how a shift can be made from water-intensive crops towards drought-tolerant crops. They said that to reach the young generation, it is necessary to show the correct picture of Ethanol through reels, short videos and ground-level meetings.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan listened to suggestions and gave guidance

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan listened carefully to the farmers throughout and kept asking questions in between to understand the ground situation. He said that the thought process of the Central Government is clear – the benefit of the Ethanol programme should reach the entire chain, from the field to the fuel tank, but the largest share should go in the interest of the farmer. Shri Shivraj Chouhan said that Ethanol will strengthen the country’s energy security as well as the farmers’ pockets. Our emphasis is on ensuring that no crop and no state faces injustice.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan gave the assurance in the meeting that the policy will be reviewed to maintain the balance of prices and demand of maize, rice, sugarcane and other feedstocks. Decisions will be taken only from the point of view of farmer interest, especially the benefit of maize farmers. Through the scientific studies and technical reports available on Ethanol, the negative narrative will be answered, and fact-based dialogue will be carried forward together with the farmers.

Farmers’ views, Minister’s guidance – Message of partnership

At the end of the meeting, the representatives of AIKCC said that they will take this message to the villages that the confusion regarding Ethanol will be broken on the basis of facts and ground experience, and the process of making policy in the interest of farmers will be strengthened by working together with the government. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also gave a clear message that farmer organisations are not opponents of the government but partners in policy. He said that we have carefully listened to the farmers’ views on Ethanol; now our work is to create such a framework on the basis of these suggestions in which the farmer, the country and energy – all three become strong.

The AIKCC delegation included National President of AIKCC and former MP from Bharatiya Kisan Union (Mann) Shri Bhupinder Singh Mann, National Vice-President of AIKCC and President of National Association for Farmer Producer Organisations (NAFPO) Shri Binod Anand, National Vice-President of AIKCC Shri Gurusahib Singh Mann, National General Secretary of AIKCC and trainer of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Gunwat Patil, Member of AIKCC and National General Secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union Mann and President of Kisan Union Mann (UP) Shri Ajay Anmol, Member of AIKCC and Vice-President of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Lalit Bahale Patil, Member of AIKCC and National General Secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union Mann (Haryana) Shri Balraj Singh Sandhu, Member of AIKCC and President of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Surjit Singh Mani Gurjar, Member of AIKCC and State Vice-President of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Jugnu Rana, Member of AIKCC and State General Secretary of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Manphool Singh, Member of AIKCC and President of Vyamalan Kisan Sangathan (Tamil Nadu) Shri V. Manikkam, Member of AIKCC and President of Kisan Jagaran (Telangana) Shri Sugunakar Rao, Member of AIKCC and President of BKU Mann (Chandigarh) Shri Balwant Singh Nadiyali, Member of AIKCC and Spokesperson of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Dinesh Sharma, Member of AIKCC and President of Malwa BKU Mann Shri Balveer Singh, and Member of AIKCC Shri Shivaraj Singh.

headline: Union Minister Scindia, MP CM Mohan Yadav Secure Cumulative ₹5,500 Crore Investment Commitments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister Scindia, MP CM Mohan Yadav Secure Cumulative ₹5,500 Crore Investment Commitments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone

Mumbai Investors’ Meet Attracts Fresh ₹2,000 Crore Commitments; Telecom Manufacturing Zone Set to Generate over 18,000 Employment Opportunities

India Advancing Towards a Global Standard, Best-in-Class Manufacturing Ecosystem Led By PM Modi: Scindia

04 AUG 2026 8:20PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai : 4 August 2026

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, along with Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, today co-chaired the second Investors’ Meet in Mumbai for India’s first and only Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, securing fresh investment commitments worth ₹2,000 crore for the initiative. The meeting witnessed participation from nearly 18 leading industry players from across the telecom ecosystem, with the latest commitments expected to generate close to 4,000 employment opportunities.

With the Mumbai commitments, the Telecom Manufacturing Zone has now attracted cumulative investment commitments worth ₹5,500 crore and is expected to create over 18,000 employment opportunities. This builds upon the ₹3,500 crore investment commitments and 14,000 jobs announced during the inaugural Investors’ Roundtable in New Delhi held last week, marking another significant milestone towards the TMZ’s vision of attracting over ₹10,000 crore in investments.

Addressing industry leaders, Minister Scindia said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has witnessed a transformational revolution in telecommunications and digitalisation over the last twelve years. He noted that India has evolved from a nation driven by telecom services into one preparing to become a global leader in telecom products and manufacturing.

Emphasising the vision of “Make in India, Make for the World” and “Local for Global”, the Minister said India must now transition from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. He outlined a three-pronged strategy to achieve this transformation: increasing domestic value addition, creating intellectual property in India, and enabling Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured telecom products to reach every corner of the world.

Drawing parallels with India’s remarkable success in mobile manufacturing and digital public infrastructure, Minister Scindia said that the same model can now be replicated in telecom manufacturing. He noted that India has transformed from importing the vast majority of its mobile phones to becoming one of the world’s largest mobile manufacturing hubs, while digital platforms such as UPI have demonstrated India’s ability to create globally scalable technology solutions. He expressed confidence that the TMZ in Gwalior would emerge as another global success story that countries around the world could look to replicate.

The Minister described the Telecom Manufacturing Zone as a first-of-its-kind initiative inspired by the success of Special Economic Zones but designed exclusively for the telecommunications sector. The integrated ecosystem will bring together the complete telecom value chain, including design, research and development, testing, manufacturing, components, semiconductors, optical fibre, telecom equipment and allied industries, supported by common plug-and-play testing infrastructure and world-class facilities.

Highlighting Gwalior’s strategic advantages, Minister Scindia said its central location, excellent connectivity, established industrial ecosystem, availability of plug-and-play infrastructure, strong talent pipeline from premier educational institutions, and competitive operating costs make it an ideal destination for telecom manufacturing investments. Highlighting Gwalior’s rapidly evolving infrastructure, Minister Scindia noted that enhanced connectivity is significantly strengthening the city’s investment proposition. He said that with the upcoming high-speed Agra-Gwalior Greenfield Expressway and improved highway connectivity to the NCR, travel between Delhi-NCR and Gwalior will be completed in less than 3 hours.

He invited companies across every telecom vertical to establish operations in the Zone, creating a complete end-to-end manufacturing ecosystem.

The Minister also praised Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Government of Madhya Pradesh for their proactive partnership in making the Telecom Manufacturing Zone a reality. He highlighted the State’s industry-friendly incentives, including land availability, capital support, employment-linked incentives, skill development assistance and logistics advantages, which together make the project globally competitive.

Reaffirming the Government’s long-term commitment, Minister Scindia announced that a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) comprising representatives from both the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh will jointly steer the implementation of the project. Calling it an unprecedented Centre-State partnership, he assured investors that both governments would work together continuously to resolve issues, facilitate investments and ensure the long-term success of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

The Investors’ Meet was attended by Secretary, Department of Telecommunications Amit Agarwal, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh Neeraj Mandloi, senior government officials, industry leaders and investors from across the telecommunications ecosystem.

headline: Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026

04 AUG 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

On 04.08.2026, Air India Flight AI2379, operated by an Airbus A320 aircraft (VT-EXO) from Phuket to Delhi, experienced a momentary altitude variation during flight. The aircraft subsequently stabilised and landed safely at Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi.

The flight was carrying 137 passengers, including 3 infants, and 8 crew members (2 pilots and 6 cabin crew).

Immediately upon landing, medical teams attended to all passengers and crew as a precautionary measure. Eight passengers and four cabin crew members have been admitted to hospitals for detailed medical evaluation and treatment. All admitted passengers and crew members are stable and are being provided with adequate medical care and attention. The remaining passengers were provided the necessary assistance and support.

Hon’ble Minister of Civil Aviation personally visited Fortis Hospital, accompanied by the Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation and DG DGCA to enquire about the condition of the injured passengers and assure them of all necessary assistance. Senior officers of the Ministry have also visited Fortis and Medanta Hospitals and are closely coordinating with the hospital authorities and the airline to ensure the best possible medical care and all necessary support to the injured.

The aircraft has been moved to the hangar and the Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder have been secured for detailed examination.

DGCA has initiated a detailed investigation into the occurrence. The Ministry of Civil Aviation and DGCA are closely monitoring the situation. Passenger safety remains the highest priority, and all necessary measures are being taken.

headline: Government Strengthens Livestock Development, Dairy Productivity and Animal Health Across the Country
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Government Strengthens Livestock Development, Dairy Productivity and Animal Health Across the Country

Promoting Piggery Development and Livestock Entrepreneurship in Assam

Improving Dairy Productivity and Strengthening Fodder Security

Strengthening Animal Disease Control and Veterinary Infrastructure

05 AUG 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, today informed the Rajya Sabha that the Government of India is implementing a series of focused initiatives to strengthen livestock development, improve dairy productivity, enhance animal health, and promote sustainable rural livelihoods across the country. Through flagship schemes such as the National Livestock Mission (NLM), Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) and Livestock Health & Disease Control Programme (LHDCP), the Government is supporting infrastructure creation, scientific breeding, disease control, fodder development and entrepreneurship in the livestock sector.

The Minister informed that entrepreneurs in Assam are being supported under the National Livestock Mission and the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund to establish modern pig breeding farms and pork processing units. During the last three years, subsidy of ₹4.98 crore has been released for 50 livestock projects, including 23 pig breeding farms, under the Entrepreneurship Development Programme of NLM. Under AHIDF, ₹1.44 crore has been released as interest subvention for eight projects, including one pig breeding farm.

Further, ₹41.67 crore has been released under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission for bovine genetic improvement, ₹124.29 crore under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme, and ₹7.74 crore under the National Livestock Mission for various livestock development activities during 2024-25 and 2025-26.

To strengthen scientific pig breeding, the Government has sanctioned ₹1.80 crore for establishing a Pig Semen Collection and Processing Laboratory in Assam to promote artificial insemination and genetic improvement. The Department has also published "Good Husbandry Practices in Pig Farming" to encourage scientific pig farming. In addition, 9,92,863 Classical Swine Fever vaccinations have been administered free of cost in the State, supporting disease control, employment generation and export potential.

The Minister stated that India's average bovine milk productivity has increased from 1,648 kg per animal per year in 2014-15 to 2,251 kg in 2024-25, while national milk production has risen by 70 per cent, from 146 million metric tonnes to 248 million metric tonnes over the same period.

To address fodder shortages, the Government is implementing multiple interventions under the National Livestock Mission, including quality fodder seed production and support for hay, silage and Total Mixed Ration (TMR) infrastructure. During the last five years, ₹1,152.40 crore has been released, resulting in the production of 1.6 lakh tonnes of quality fodder seed. Under NLM-EDP, 204 fodder-related projects have been approved, while AHIDF has supported 174 animal feed plants with investments of ₹3,602.47 crore.

The Minister further informed that 100 dedicated Fodder-Plus Farmer Producer Organisations have been established by the National Dairy Development Board, while ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute has developed high-yielding forage varieties, state-specific fodder development plans and trained over 10 lakh farmers. The Government has also issued heatwave management guidelines to States and Union Territories and continues to promote indigenous cattle breeds known for their resilience to high temperatures. Digital advisory services are being provided through the 1962 Farmers App under Bharat Pashudhan, enabling farmers to adopt scientific ration balancing practices.

Replying to a separate question on Andhra Pradesh, the Minister informed that under the National Animal Disease Control Programme, implemented as part of the Livestock Health & Disease Control Programme, the Government provides 100 percent Central assistance for vaccination against Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) and Brucellosis.

headline: REFORMS IN COAL SECTOR
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

REFORMS IN COAL SECTOR

05 AUG 2026 1:58PM by PIB Delhi

Over the last five years, the Government has carried out a series of structural and procedural reforms to make coal allocation and mining more transparent, efficient, and scientific. The key change has been the shift from allotment to allocation through open competitive auction, alongside the opening of commercial coal mining in 2020 with no restriction on the sale or end-use of coal.

1. Key Reforms for Transparency and Market-Based Allocation:

Commercial Coal Mining: Opened with no technical or financial eligibility conditions, and 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) has been allowed under the automatic route.

Revenue-Share Model: Auctions have migrated to a percentage revenue-share model, supported by the introduction of the National Coal Index for transparent, market-linked pricing.

Single Window Mode Agnostic (SWMA) Auction: Introduced to sell all non-linkage coal of Coal India Limited (CIL) through a single window, removing market distortions and enhancing fair competition amongst buyers.

SHAKTI Policy Simplification: Coal linkage allocation has been simplified into two windows—Window I at Notified Price and Window II at a Premium above Notified Price, enabling existing linkage consumers to procure up to 100% PLF requirement.

CoalSETU Window: Introduced under the Non-Regulated Sector (NRS) Linkage Auction Policy to provide auction-based linkages without end-use restrictions, allowing full flexibility for self-consumption, coal washing, or export.

2. Reforms for Efficiency and Ease of Doing Business:

Single Window Clearance System: Introduced through the PARIVESH 2.0 portal for faster mine operationalization.

Exploration: 44 private entities have been notified as Accredited Prospecting Agencies (APA), removing the need for a prospecting license. The Geological Reports approval mechanism has also been simplified.

Statutory Amendments: The Colliery Control Rules have been amended to empower coal company boards to accord Mine Opening Permissions. Furthermore, Coking Coal has been notified as a Critical and Strategic Mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957, thereby, expediting Environment Clearance and Forest Clearance process for Coking Coal Projects

Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) Mode: The Government has introduced the Mine Developer and Operator mode for coal mining and has also offered closed/abandoned mines under a revenue-sharing model to maximize resource extraction.

Insurance Surety Bond has been included as an acceptable instrument for furnishing Performance Security in the Coal Block Development and Production Agreements. This will reduce dependence on Bank Guarantees, release blocked working capital and widen participation.

The Government has taken several initiatives to modernise the coal ecosystem through technology adoption and clean coal initiatives:

Coal Washing: Under 'Mission Coking Coal', the Government aims to enhance the country's coal washery capacity to 58 MT by FY 2030.

Digital Mine Monitoring: The Ministry of Coal has launched the Koyla Shakti Dashboard for real-time monitoring of coal production, dispatch, stocks, and transportation. Additionally, the Khanan Prahari mobile app and CMSMS web app have been deployed nationally for citizen-based reporting of unauthorized mining activities. CIL has also deployed Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCC) with AI-based video analytics, RFID-enabled weighbridges, GPS-based vehicle tracking, and drone/satellite-based mapping for scientific mine planning.

Coal Gasification & UCG: To promote surface coal/lignite gasification, the Government has approved two major schemes with financial outlays of ₹8,500 crore (under which 8 projects are already approved) and ₹37,500 crore to meet the target of 100 MT gasification capacity by 2030.

Renewable Energy & Carbon Capture: CIL has adopted a phased renewable energy roadmap with a target of 3 GW of net-zero renewable capacity by FY 2027-28 and 9.5 GW by FY 2029-30, with 558 MW already installed across utility and captive projects.

Coal continues to play a vital role in meeting the country's energy needs and supporting industrial growth.

Further, the Government promotes environmental sustainability in coal mining through initiatives such as plantation/bio-reclamation, development of eco-parks, and mine water utilization. Blast-free mining technologies (like Surface Miners) are being aggressively adopted to replace conventional drilling.

India’s domestic coal production has increased significantly from about 731 million tonnes in 2019-20 to cross 1 Billion Tonnes for two consecutive years, reaching 1047.52 MT in FY 2024-25 and 1039 MT in FY 2025-26.

The Government has launched an Integrated Coal Logistics Plan aiming to develop a technology-enabled, cost-effective multimodal logistics ecosystem through rail, road, coastal shipping, and inland waterways. A total of 139 First Mile Connectivity (FMC) projects with an aggregate capacity of about 1,319 million tonnes have been taken up, out of which 72 projects with a capacity of about 589 million tonnes have already been commissioned

To further streamline the sector, the Government has notified the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026 to establish a regulated online platform for trading coal and its processed forms. The Coal Exchange will enable captive/commercial miners and consumers to enter into delivery-based contracts.

This information was given by Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Preparedness for EI Nino Conditions
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Preparedness for EI Nino Conditions

05 AUG 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi

India Meteorological Department (IMD) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences assesses the likely impact of El Niño on the Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall. In general, during the El Nino event, the Indian summer monsoon is weaker than normal, and the intensity of the El Nino also decides the amount of impact on the monsoon. Since 1950, there have been 16 El Niño years, out of which 7 years had impacted Indian monsoon rainfall when rainfall was below normal. However, there is a stronger inverse relationship between El Niño and rainfall during the later half of the monsoon season (particularly with September rainfall).

The IMD regularly issues seasonal and monthly forecasts for rainfall and temperature. IMD issued a below-normal rainfall forecast for the 2026 Southwest Monsoon season. In its First Stage Long Range Forecast, issued on 13 April 2026, IMD predicted the seasonal rainfall to be 92% of the Long Period Average (LPA) with a model error of ±5%. Subsequently, in the Second Stage Long Range Forecast, IMD revised the seasonal rainfall forecast to 90% of the LPA with a model error of ±4%. IMD also indicated the likely development of El Niño conditions during the Southwest Monsoon season in its seasonal forecasts, thereby providing advance guidance for preparedness and planning by the concerned stakeholders.

In addition, IMD provides regular updates on monsoon rainfall at daily intervals and El Nino conditions at monthly intervals. IMD also provides rainfall at district and block levels to all stakeholders and participates in meetings conducted by PMO, MHA, MoAFW regularly and provides relevant inputs. Under crop weather watch of MoAFW every week, IMD provides past rainfall and forecast of rainfall for the next two weeks.

Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), MoES, based on the experimental forecast of 2026 in the seasonal to short and medium range, is working with Agriculture and dam management departments to provide the impact of rainfall and developing ENSO in agriculture and water management

Ministry of Earth Sciences has not issued any district-wise risk and impact assessment study or guidelines to the States regarding tackling the impacts of El Niño during 2026.

However, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, regularly issues weather and climate forecasts, seasonal outlooks, and early warnings related to rainfall, heatwaves, and other extreme weather events, which are disseminated to all concerned Central Ministries, State Governments, and other stakeholders to support preparedness and appropriate response measures.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ADVANCING MONSOON SCIENCE, CLIMATE RESEARCH AND WEATHER FORECASTING
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ADVANCING MONSOON SCIENCE, CLIMATE RESEARCH AND WEATHER FORECASTING

05 AUG 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi

Recent studies have shown an increase in the frequency of deep convective clouds and in more intense, short-duration extreme rainfall. A recent study using satellite data showed a significant increase in the cloud top height of deep convective clouds as well as increases in the frequency of occurrence of deep convective clouds over the Indian subcontinent and adjacent oceanic regions (https://doi.org/10.1029/2024GL111394). A significant rising trend in the frequency and the magnitude of extreme rain events, and a significant decreasing trend in the frequency of moderate events over central India have also been studied (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1132027). The long-term changes in low cloud across the country have also been assessed by IMD (https://doi.org/10.54302/mausam.v68i2.627). The impact of human-induced global climate change on the regional climate and monsoons of the Indian subcontinent, adjoining Indian Ocean and the Himalayas has been studied in detail by the MoES scientists (https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-15-4327-2).

The Mission Mausam was envisaged with the sole purpose of creating an integrated framework for strengthening climate modelling, satellite observations, atmospheric research and numerical weather prediction to improve understanding of changing monsoon patterns and associated extreme weather events, including:

Adoption of advanced Multi-Model Ensemble (MME) and coupled dynamical climate models for operational long-range forecasting at monthly and seasonal scale for every month and season.

Continuous upgradation of Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models through improved model physics, higher spatial resolution, advanced data assimilation techniques and enhanced computational capabilities.

Strengthening of the national meteorological observation network through the installation of additional Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs), lightning network, Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs), Automatic Rain Gauges (ARGs), upper-air observing systems, wind profilers and other observing platforms.

Expansion of satellite-based observations through indigenous meteorological satellites and assimilation of satellite, radar and in-situ observations for improving forecast accuracy. National Centre For Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) routinely receives near-real-time satellite observations from major global satellite data providers, including NASA/NOAA, ESA/EUMETCast, CMA, KMA, and JMA, in addition to data from the national agencies ISRO and IMD. The Centre has established the necessary infrastructure to receive and assimilate newly operational international satellite observations designated as WMO Core Data, ensuring their timely utilization in operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) data assimilation systems.

Development of indigenous, technology-driven, and citizen-centric weather forecasting systems that strengthen disaster preparedness and improve public safety across India. IMD’s in-house developed Decision Support System (DSS) is a major step in the direction of promoting self-reliance under the “Atmanirbhar Bharat” initiative.

Dissemination of weather forecasts and warnings through multiple communication platforms, including mobile applications, APIs, web portals, SMS, television, radio and social media, in coordination with Central and State Government agencies.

In collaboration with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, IMD has developed the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, providing Panchayat-level weather forecasts through e-GramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), Meri Panchayat App, e-Manchitra and Mausamgram (https://mausamgram.imd.gov.in). The mobile numbers of Panchayat Members, Ward Members and Panchayat Secretaries have been integrated with the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, enabling timely dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories through WhatsApp for further dissemination at the Gram Panchayat level. IMD also leverages the Krishi Sakhis and Pashu Sakhis network of the Ministry of Rural Development for last-mile dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

NCMRWF has developed two state-of-the-art climate reanalysis datasets: a global reanalysis covering 1992–2018 at 25 km horizontal resolution (NGFS) and a regional reanalysis covering 1979–2020 at 12 km horizontal resolution (IMDAA). These long-term, high-resolution datasets provide a valuable foundation for climate diagnostics, variability studies, and the development of AI/ML based climate applications at both national and international levels. The bias-corrected reanalysis products play a crucial role in the robust assessment of climate variability and extremes, including heatwaves, cold waves, cyclones, and heavy rainfall events. Building on these achievements.

The Mission Mausam Program of the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) is assisting implementation of Higher-resolution atmospheric observations, Next-generation radars, High-Performance Computers (HPC), developing improved earth system models and data-driven methods (use of AI/ML), developing a state-of-the-art Decision Support System (DSS) and dissemination system for last-mile connectivity.

Under Mission Mausam, extra-mural projects are awarded to academic and research institutes across India and abroad for advancing monsoon research and prediction. IMD coordinates with national and international institutions to strengthen monsoon science, improve weather and climate prediction, and enhance climate resilience. The major collaborative initiatives include:

Collaboration with academic and research institutions, including the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), universities and other national research organizations, for research on monsoon dynamics, climate variability, numerical weather prediction and extreme weather events.

Active participation in programmes of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and collaboration with international meteorological and climate research organizations for exchange of scientific knowledge, observational data, modelling techniques and best practices.

Cooperation with national agencies engaged in Earth system science for strengthening weather and climate services through improved observations, modelling, forecasting and impact-based early warning systems.

Joint research, capacity building, training programmes, workshops and scientific exchanges with national and international institutions to advance understanding of monsoon processes and improve forecasting capabilities.

Continuous engagement with Central and State Government agencies, research institutions and disaster management authorities to translate scientific advances into improved climate resilience and weather-related risk reduction.

Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) is using the latest version of the Monsoon Mission forecast system now. The plan is to improve the seasonal prediction model with in-house developed oceanic fluxes, inclusion of a new land surface model, river routing, etc as modified components of the seasonal prediction system. This is supposed to improve the skill of the model not only in predicting the all-India rainfall, but also its usefulness for applications such as extreme weather predictions during the monsoon period.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER-BASED AGRO-ADVISOR SERVICES
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER-BASED AGRO-ADVISOR SERVICES

05 AUG 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has undertaken several measures to strengthen the country's weather forecasting system through the India Meteorological Department (IMD) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). It has adopted advanced, state-of-the-art technologies, including high-performance computing (HPC) facilities to support high-resolution Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models, modern observational networks, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled weather forecasting tools. These advancements have significantly enhanced the accuracy and reliability of weather monitoring, forecasting, and early warning services across the country. Currently, the Ministry has a weather observation network comprising manual observatories, Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs), Automated Rain Gauges (ARGs), Agro-AWS, Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs), upper-air observatories, and weather monitoring satellites.

Under Mission Mausam, various global and regional NWP modeling systems have been implemented and operationalized to generate seamless short-, medium-, and extended-range forecasts for all, including farmers. The Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS), with a spatial resolution of 6 km, generates forecasts at the cluster of Panchayat level, enabling the capture of localized weather features and improving the accuracy of weather forecasts.

India Meteorological Department, in collaboration with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR), has launched Panchayat-level weather forecasts covering nearly all Gram Panchayats in India. These forecasts are accessible through digital platforms such as e-Gramswaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), Meri Panchayat app, e-Manchitra of MoPR, and Mausamgram of IMD, MoES (https://mausamgram.imd.gov.in). Currently, three AI-based global models (e.g., Pangu Weather, FourCastNet, GraphCast) are operational to provide guidance to the forecaster to predict severe weather. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) applications and tools have been developed indigenously by weather scientists of the MoES institutions for various aspects of monitoring and observational processing, such as the Nowcasting tool and downscaled urban forecasting.

IMD implements the Gramin Krishi Mausam Sewa (GKMS) in collaboration with 55 Host Institutes, including the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), and other institutions. Under this, 130 Agrometeorological Field Units (AMFUs) covering 127 agro-climatic zones issue district-specific agro-meteorological advisories twice (Tuesday and Friday) a week ahead, based on IMD's medium-range weather forecasts, and communicate to the farmers. Under the GKMS scheme, all agriculturally important districts are covered across the country, including Uttar Pradesh, for providing real-time weather forecasts, agro-meteorological advisories, and early warnings directly to the farmers. In addition, IMD issues district-level impact-based weather forecast & risk-based warning valid up to 7 days through Regional Meteorological Centres & Meteorological Centres for their concerned States, including Uttar Pradesh twice daily. These warnings are issued more frequently in case of severe weather. Dissemination of weather forecasts and warnings through multiple communication platforms, including mobile applications, APIs, web portals, SMS, television, radio, and social media, in coordination with Central and State Government agencies.

IMD developed a public-friendly website (https://mausam.imd.gov.in/) and mobile apps for the dissemination of weather-related warnings, such as the MAUSAM App for weather forecasting and warnings, MEGHDOOT App for agro-meteorological services, the DAMINI App for lightning warnings, UMANG App for weather forecasting and warnings across the country, including Baghpat, Western Uttar Pradesh. Further, IMD regularly conducts the survey to assess the usefulness of the products for specific sectors like agro-advisory services to farmers and nowcast services for the general public. Based on the survey findings, a report has been prepared and released. The report is publicly available at the following links: https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/contents/agromet/kalp/voices.pdf & https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/contents/agromet/states/States.pdf.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPACT AND ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE DEEP OCEAN MISSION
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPACT AND ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE DEEP OCEAN MISSION

05 AUG 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi

Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) is a flagship initiative launched by the Government of India in 2021, encompassing activities across six verticals. These verticals are (1) Development of Technologies for Deep-sea mining, Human Submersible and underwater robotics, (2) Development of Ocean Climate Change Advisory Services, (3) Technological Innovations for exploration and conservation of deep-sea biodiversity, (4) Deep-ocean survey and exploration, (5) Energy and fresh water from the ocean, and (6) Establishment of Advanced Marine Station for Ocean Biology. The research and activities under the Mission aim to explore and harness ocean living and non-living resources (such as biodiversity, polymetallic nodules, polymetallic sulphides, and ocean thermal energy) as part of the pilot project for developing India’s Blue Economy.

The notable achievements made under the Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) are as follows:

DOM Vertical: Thematic area | Progress

Vertical 1: Development of technologies for manned submersible, deep-sea mining and underwater vehicles and underwater robotics | The design and system engineering for India’s flagship human submersible, MATSYA-6000, are complete; subsystems have been realised; and crewed and uncrewed wet harbour trials at 8m depth were conducted from 22nd January 2025 to 14th February 2025 at Kattupalli, near Chennai. Scientists at the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, entrusted with the development of MATSYA-6000, have gained pilot experience with the French submersible NAUTILE in August 2025. The design of the self-propelled deep-sea nodule collector/deep-sea mining machine is complete, and a successful demonstration of the collection of over 100 kg of Cobalt-rich deep-sea polymetallic nodules from a depth of 1173m was conducted in the Andaman Sea in 2024.

Vertical 2: Development of ocean climate change advisory services | A suite of ocean models for downscaling sea level, wave, storm surge, and biogeochemical projections of the Indian Ocean; prediction of 100-year extreme sea level along the coasts of the Indian subcontinent and associated coastal vulnerability maps; Genesis Potential Index for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal; and a wave model for Indian Ocean wave climate analysis have been completed. To strengthen ocean observation, the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Hyderabad, has successfully completed 11 glider missions in the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, and deployed 60 directional Wave Spectra Barometric Drifters and 92 physical and biogeochemical Argo floats in the Indian Ocean.

Vertical 3: Technological innovations for exploration and conservation of deep-sea biodiversity | Detailed profiling and characterisation studies, including genomic analysis, screening for industrially useful molecules, and the preservation of select deep-sea microbial samples, have been conducted. Nearly 2038 deep-sea microbes have been isolated from water and sediment samples in the Indian EEZ, and rare deep-sea microbes previously unreported from the Indian Ocean have been discovered. A Marine Microbial Repository is being established at Chittedu, Andhra Pradesh. Nearly 31 seamounts (biodiversity hotspots) in the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal have been surveyed by the Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE), Kochi, which documented 201 deep-sea species, including 43 potentially new to science.

Vertical 4: Deep ocean survey and exploration (and research ship) | Deep-sea expeditions in the Central and Southwest Indian Ridges have been conducted, leading to the discovery of four hydrothermal vent fields and two inactive vents (potential mineralised zones), including India’s first imaging of an active vent. A contract has been awarded to GRSE, Kolkata (a PSU under the Ministry of Defence), for the indigenous construction of a new multipurpose, all-weather ocean research vessel. The design of the new oceanographic research vessel, model tests, and keel laying have been completed.

Vertical 5: Energy and freshwater from the ocean | A detailed project report for a high-capacity offshore Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC)-powered desalination plant has been prepared.

Vertical 6: Advanced Marine Station for Ocean Biology | Land for setting up the Advanced Marine Station in Nemmeli, Chennai, has been procured. 145 collaborative research projects with nearly 70 national institutions, including universities, colleges, and laboratories, are ongoing across various areas of ocean/marine sciences.

For deep-sea resource exploration and utilisation, the draft Mining Code of the International Seabed Authority (ISA) incorporates stringent environmental safeguards, including the precautionary approach, environmental baseline studies, environmental impact assessments (EIAs), environmental management and monitoring programmes, and adaptive management measures to protect the marine environment. India participates in the consultative approach implemented by the ISA to develop these safeguards. The Mining Code has yet to be ratified by the ISA.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs

FOREST RIGHTS ACT

05 AUG 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed the Rajya Sabha today that As per the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (in short, FRA) and Rules made thereunder, State Governments and UT Administrations are responsible for implementation of various provisions of the Act while the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) compiles Monthly Progress Report (MPR) received from the States/UTs. As per the information reported by States/UTs and collated under MPR during FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26 i.e. from 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2026, a total of 8,56,159 claims (8,21,908 Individual & 34,251 Community claims) have been filed, a total of 2,34,352 claims (2,18,899 Individual & 15,453 Community claims) have been approved/ titles distributed and a total of 14,462 claims (13,756 Individual & 706 Community claims) have been rejected. The state-wise details are available on MoTA’s website at https://tribal.nic.in/FRA.aspx.

Forest Rights Act and its rules, does not prescribe a time-limit for disposal of claim filed and no such information is centrally maintained by MoTA.

Based on the information received from some of the State Governments, the major reasons for the rejection of claims are - claimed land not occupied before 13th December 2005, duplicate claims filed on the same land, claims on Non-Forest Land, lack of evidence, etc.

headline: PARTICIPATION OF TRIBAL WOMEN IN VDVKs

Ministry of Tribal Affairs

PARTICIPATION OF TRIBAL WOMEN IN VDVKs

05 AUG 2026 12:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed the Rajya Sabha today that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, through TRIFED, is implementing two schemes, namely Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), to strengthen entrepreneurship initiatives and facilitate livelihood opportunities for tribal men and women through more efficient, equitable and self-managed use of natural resources, MFPs, and farm & non-farm tribal product-based enterprises. A typical PMJVM VDVK comprises 15 Self-Help Groups (SHGs) with 20 beneficiaries each, while a PM-JANMAN VDVK comprises 5 SHGs with 10 beneficiaries each. Under the PMJVM scheme, 4,172 VDVKs associating 12.48 lakh beneficiaries, including tribal women beneficiaries, have been sanctioned in 28 States/UTs. Under the PM-JANMAN scheme, 540 VDVKs associating 0.46 lakh beneficiaries, including tribal women beneficiaries, have been sanctioned in 18 States/UTs. Out of these, the beneficiaries of 2,922 VDVKs, covering 7.13 lakh beneficiaries (including both men and women), have been imparted training in sustainable collection of Minor Forest Produce (MFP), agricultural produce and allied livelihood activities, primary processing, value addition, packaging, branding, and marketing of products, thereby strengthening their skills and market linkages. Moreover, 3,406 VDVKs are operational and have collectively sold value-added products worth approximately Rs. 174 crore through local markets, fairs (melas) and the Bharat Tribes Fest (BTF), thereby enhancing income generation, promoting sustainable livelihoods and fostering entrepreneurship among tribal communities, including tribal women.

headline: Socio-Economic Development and Welfare of Scheduled Tribes
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Socio-Economic Development and Welfare of Scheduled Tribes

05 AUG 2026 12:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed the Rajya Sabha today that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements several major schemes for the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes. A brief of each scheme, together with State/UT-wise funds released and physical outcomes achieved during the last five financial years, is given below and at the Annexure:

(i) Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) — Objective: to provide quality residential education, up to Class XII and on par with Navodaya Vidyalayas, to ST students, with one school envisaged for every block having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons. Status: against a target of 728 schools, 479 are functional, with cumulative enrolment rising from 92,075 (2020-21) to 1,38,336 (2024-25). Year-wise funds released, approved/functional status, and enrolment, State/UT-wise, are at Annexure I(A) to I(C).

(ii) Pre-Matric Scholarship for STs — Objective: financial assistance to ST students studying in Classes IX and X to reduce drop-out and encourage continuation of schooling. State/UT-wise funds released and number of beneficiaries for the last five years are at Annexure II.

(iii) Post-Matric Scholarship for STs — Objective: financial assistance to ST students pursuing post-matriculation and post-secondary studies to enable completion of higher education. State/UT-wise funds released and number of beneficiaries for the last five years are at Annexure III.

(iv) PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjan Jati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan) — Objective: launched on 15.11.2023 for saturation of basic facilities among Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) through convergence of 9 line Ministries, including provision of Multi-Purpose Centres (MPCs) for livelihood and skill infrastructure. State-wise funds released for MPCs are at Annexure IV.

(v) PM-JANMAN — Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) — Objective: livelihood and skill-training centres for PVTG beneficiaries, centred on minor forest produce (MFP)-based value addition. Status: 540 VDVKs sanctioned, benefiting 46,042 persons; State-wise details are at Annexure V.

(vi) Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) — Van Dhan Vikas Kendras — Objective: promotion of MFP-based livelihoods for tribal gatherers through Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (value-addition and processing clusters) under the Van Dhan Yojana component of PMJVM. Status: 4,172 VDVKs sanctioned, benefiting 12,48,067 members; State-wise funds sanctioned/released are at Annexure VI.

(vii) Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) — Objective: dedicated support for the socio-economic development of the 75 identified PVTGs, covering habitat, health, education, and livelihood needs. State-wise funds released for the last five years are at Annexure VII.

(viii) Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution — Objective: Constitutional grant-in-aid to States for promoting the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas to that of the rest of the State. State-wise funds released for the last five years are at Annexure VIII.

(ix) National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) — Objective: apex financial institution providing concessional credit for livelihood and income-generating activities to ST beneficiaries below double the poverty line. State-wise loan disbursement and number of beneficiaries are at Annexure IX.

(x) Grant-in-Aid to Non-Governmental/Voluntary Organisations working for ST welfare — Objective: financial assistance to voluntary organisations undertaking educational, health, and livelihood activities for Scheduled Tribes. State-wise funds released and beneficiaries are at Annexure X.

(xi) Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) — Objective: assistance to State Tribal Research Institutes for research, documentation, and capacity-building on tribal issues, to inform policy-making. State-wise funds released for the last five years are at Annexure XI& XII.

(xii)Tribal Research, Information Education, Communication and Events(TRI-ECE) scheme-

The Scheme provides for recognition of reputed universities , national institutions and organisations as Centre of Excellence(CoEs) for undertaking specialized research, documentation, evaluation of tribal welfare programmes and capacity-building initiatives. The studies cover diverse thematic areas, including tribal livelihoods, health and nutrition, traditional healing practices, education, digital inclusion, customary laws, and documentation of tribal art, culture, oral traditions and languages. The Scheme also supports Information, and awareness initiatives, and grants-in aid for research and documentation projects.

(xiii) Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) — Objective: launched in 2024, subsuming PMAAGY, for holistic and saturation-mode development of tribal-majority villages and habitations across the country through convergence of 17 Ministries/Departments and 25 interventions covering over 63,000 villages. State-wise funds released for 2024-25 and 2025-26 are at Annexure XIII.

The current Status and measurable outputs achieved under the schemes are as follows:

A total pf 3,505 activities/projects have been sanctioned/undertaken across States/Uts with a cumulative financial outlay of approximately Rs.1,072.31 crore.

1,188 Research and Documentation studies have been undertaken covering tribal arts, crafts, cuisine, traditional medicine. folklore, customary practices and languages.

868 Training, seminars, workshop and conference programmes have been conducted for capacity building and knowledge dissemination.

19 Tribal museum construction/renovation projects and 121 Tribal research Institute building construction/renovation projects have been sanctioned to strengthen institutional infrastructure.

More than 75 institutions/organisations have been engaged as Centre of Excellence(CoE’s)

More than 100 research, documentations, evaluation and capacity building projects have been undertaken covering thematic areas such as tribal livelihoods, health and nutrition, education, digital inclusion, customary laws and tribal art, culture, oral traditions and languages.

An online monitoring system has been put in place by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs with web address: https://stcmis.gov.in for monitoring of DAPST funds. The framework captures data directly from the Public Finance Management System (PFMS) and enables the Ministry to see the expenditure vis-à-vis allocations of different Ministries/Departments under DAPST.

For proper accounting and monitoring, and to ensure their non-divertibility to any other scheme, funds allocated under DAPST are shown by all the obligated Ministries/Departments under the minor head '796' below the functional Major Head/Sub-Major Heads in their 'Detailed Demands for Grants'.

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs convenes meetings with obligated Ministries/Departments from time to time to review implementation of the guidelines and the allocation and expenditure of DAPST funds. Concerned officers of all major schemes of the obligated Ministries/Departments are requested to attend these meetings for proper and meaningful discussion. Allocation, expenditure, and implementation of individual schemes with DAPST allocation are discussed in the review meetings. The obligated Ministries/Departments are urged to adhere to the norms prescribed by NITI Aayog for allocation of DAPST funds under schemes that provide specific benefits to STs, and to ensure full and effective utilisation of allocated funds through regular correspondence. Nodal officers are also appointed in the respective Ministries/Departments for this purpose.

The Ministry regularly reviews the implementation and utilisation of funds under DAPST through periodic meetings with the concerned Central Ministries/Departments. In addition, the progress of flagship initiatives such PM JANMAN and DAJGUA is monitored through regular review meetings to assess both financial and physical progress and to facilitate timely resolution of implementation issues.

For PM JANMAN, a dedicated digital dashboard has been developed for district-wise monitoring of key performance indicators across the converging Ministries/Departments, enabling real-time tracking of implementation and outcomes. Third-party evaluation studies of major schemes of the Ministry, including EMRS, PM-JANMAN and PMJVM, are periodically commissioned to independently assess outcomes and inform course-correction.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Scholarship dues under ST scholarship schemes

05 AUG 2026 12:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed the Rajya Sabha today that Scholarship Division, Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs is implementing the following Scholarship Schemes to promote and encourage higher education amongst ST population:

Post Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class XI and above)

National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class)

National Fellowship for ST students(NFST).

National Overseas Scholarship for ST students.

The Scholarship schemes mentioned above at Sl. No. (i) is Centrally Sponsored Scheme and implemented through respective States/UTs of the Country. The Post Matric Scholarship Scheme is an open-ended scheme wherein scholarship is given to all eligible students, without any ceiling limit on the number of selections, for pursuing studies from class 11th to post-Graduation courses whose parental income is not more than Rs. 2.5 lakh per annum. The inviting of applications, verification, selection of beneficiaries and disbursement of scholarship amount is the primary responsibility of the respective States/UTs. Based on the proposals submitted by States/UTs and after examining requisite documents & necessary compliance, the Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs releases central share of funds to States/UTs. Further, the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations disburse the scholarship amount to all the eligible ST Student's into their bank account through DBT mode. Since, these schemes are implemented by the respective States/UTs, the information regarding pending dues payable to colleges/universities is not available with this Ministry.

The National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class) mentioned at Sl.No.(ii) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented directly by the Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs. Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the selected top-class 265 Government and Non-Government Institutes in professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, Law etc. All the ST students, with their annual parental income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. The details regarding pending dues to students and colleges/universities under this scheme is given at Annexure-I.

The National Fellowship for ST students (NFST) mentioned above at Sl. No.(iii) is Central Sector Scheme implemented directly by the Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs. Central Sector Scheme fully funded by the Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs to provide fellowship to meritorious ST students for pursuing M.Phil./Ph.D. after completion of their Master's Degree. Under the Scheme, 750 fresh fellowships are awarded every year. Fellowships are released to ST students through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode after due verification and approval of certificates like continuation certificates, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency claims approved/submitted by the concerned universities/institutions. Currently, there is no pending claims forwarded by the Universities/Institutions to this Ministry for releasing the Fellowship amount under NFST.

The National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) for ST students mentioned at Sl. No.(iv) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented through the Ministry of External Aﬀairs (MEA). The scholarship amount is released to ST students/Institutes through Indian Embassies. Further, based on the vouchers/bills submitted by the MEA regarding payment made by the Embassies to the selected ST students/Institutions, the Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs reimburse the funds to MEA. At present, there is no pending dues payable to colleges, universities and other higher-education institutions on behalf of students enrolled under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) for ST students.

(c) The Ministry is continuously monitoring the status of pending payments and taking up the matter with the concerned institutions for completion of the requisite PFMS compliance, so that admissible payments may be released expeditiously to the concerned Institutes and Beneficiaries.

The Ministry is also undertaking timely verification and processing of applications received through the National Scholarship Portal, including institutional verification and Ministry-level verification, and is taking necessary steps for early resolution of deficiencies and discrepancies observed in the applications.

Component-I: Stipend @ Rs.36000/- per annum, Books & stationary @ Rs.5000/- per annuum and Laptop allowance @ Rs.45000/- once in the course. The amount under this component is directly released into the bank accounts of the selected ST students through DBT.

headline: Union Environment Minister chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Union Environment Minister chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in New Delhi

Committee deliberates on Strengthening Human–Wildlife Conflict Mitigation through Technology, Community Participation and Coordinated National Action

05 AUG 2026 12:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Parliamentary Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change met today in New Delhi, under the Chairmanship of the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav. The agenda of the meeting was to deliberate on the issue of Human–Wildlife Conflict (HWC) and the measures required for strengthening prevention, mitigation and long-term coexistence between people and wildlife. Dignitaries in attendance included Union Minister of State (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Members of Parliament as part of the Committee, besides senior officers of the Ministry, PCCFs and Chief Wild Life Wardens of participating States.

The Committee was apprised of the follow-up action taken on the directions issued during its previous meeting held on 18.12.2025. These included consultations by States and Union Territories with Members of Parliament from conflict-affected areas. During the meeting, the Ministry highlighted that conflict patterns vary across landscapes, with human–elephant conflict being predominant in several States, while conflicts involving tigers, leopards, bears, rhinoceroses, wild boars, gaurs, primates and other species require location-specific management approaches.

The Committee was informed about the establishment of the Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict (CoE-HWC) at SACON, WII South Centre, Coimbatore, announced by the Prime Minister of India, during the 7th National Board for Wildlife meeting. The Centre has been established as a national institution for scientific research, technological innovation, policy support, capacity building and community-centred approaches for effective management of human–wildlife conflict. The Committee also noted the launch of the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal on 10.07.2026, as a unified digital platform for recording conflict incidents, data management, knowledge sharing and decision support. Further, it was informed that the Regional Action Plan (RAP) on Elephant Conservation for South India has been approved.

Presentations were made by the States of Assam, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh, highlighting their conflict scenarios, mitigation measures, community participation initiatives, use of technology, institutional mechanisms and recommendations for strengthening national efforts. The experiences presented underscored the importance of landscape-specific planning, rapid response systems, habitat improvement, protection of wildlife corridors, scientific monitoring, early warning systems, community engagement and inter-State coordination.

The discussions emphasised that effective management of human–wildlife conflict requires an integrated approach combining ecological conservation with protection of human lives and livelihoods. Members deliberated upon the use of modern technologies including GIS, artificial intelligence, drones, radio telemetry and predictive analytics, while also stressing the importance of strengthening frontline capacity, improving compensation delivery, enhancing public awareness and promoting community participation in conservation.

Highlights of the Presentations made by the Six States are as below:

Assam: The Government of Assam presented its landscape-based strategy for mitigating human–wildlife conflict involving elephants, tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, wild buffalo and wild boar. The State highlighted the constitution of Zonal Human–Wildlife Conflict Risk Reduction Committees for preparing region-specific action plans focusing on habitat restoration, corridor protection, early warning systems, rapid response, community participation and livelihood diversification. The Committee appreciated the zonal planning approach and emphasised documentation of its outcomes for replication in other conflict-prone landscapes.

Karnataka: Karnataka showcased its integrated six-pillar model for predictive human-wildlife conflict management, based on engineering interventions, AI-enabled surveillance, command centres, rapid response teams, community volunteer networks and e-Parihara digital compensation systems. The State also suggested a National Human–Wildlife Conflict Mission, common Standard Operating Procedures, corridor restoration and stronger inter-State coordination for managing transboundary elephant populations. The Committee appreciated Karnataka’s technology-driven approach and recommended wider dissemination of best practices among States.

Kerala: The State highlighted its integrated institutional framework, including declaration of Human–Wildlife Conflict as a State-Specific Disaster, deployment of Rapid Response Teams and Primary Response Teams, identification of 273 conflict-affected Panchayats and implementation of community-based initiatives such as Jana Jagaratha Samitis and the SARPA volunteer programme. The State also emphasised wildlife corridor restoration, habitat management, responsible tourism and technology-enabled monitoring. The Committee noted Kerala’s strong institutional and community-based approach and encouraged continued sharing of successful interventions with other States.

Madhya Pradesh: MP presented its ‘Prevention First’ model for human–wildlife conflict mitigation integrating AI-enabled surveillance, GPS tracking, drones, Gajrakshak, rapid response teams, species-specific Standard Operating Procedures, time-bound compensation and extensive community participation through Bagh Mitra, Hathi Mitra, and Eco-Development Committees. The State also highlighted habitat management, wildlife health support and science-based species management, including translocation of conflict animals. The Committee appreciated the integration of technology, community participation and timely relief mechanisms and encouraged further strengthening of predictive conflict management.

Uttarakhand: The State presented its strategic roadmap for conflict mitigation in priority landscapes through an Integrated Command and Control Centre, 24×7 Helpline (1926), e-surveillance, GPS tracking, habitat restoration, bio-fencing, timely compensation and village-based volunteer networks. The State also outlined its long-term strategy focusing on wildlife-sensitive landscape planning, district-level monitoring committees and strengthening coexistence measures under the ‘Living with Leopards/Tigers’ initiative. The Committee appreciated Uttarakhand’s integrated landscape approach and stressed the importance of technology-enabled early warning systems and community preparedness.

Uttar Pradesh: UP highlighted that leopard-related incidents constitute the majority of human–wildlife conflict cases in the State, with the Terai Arc Landscape being the principal hotspot. The State presented its strategy based on Rapid Response Teams, rescue centres (4 constructed), solar fencing, early warning systems, community volunteer programmes, scientific monitoring and strengthened conservation interventions beyond Protected Areas. The Committee appreciated the State’s focus on scientific management and advised continued strengthening of community-based mitigation and monitoring systems in high-conflict landscapes.

Union Environment Minister, Shri Yadav, appreciated the initiatives undertaken by the States and observed that the challenge of human–wildlife conflict must be addressed through a balanced approach that combines scientific management, institutional coordination, technology-enabled monitoring and active involvement of local communities. He emphasised that the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal and the Centre of Excellence would provide an important institutional framework for developing data-driven strategies, facilitating knowledge exchange and supporting States in adopting best practices. Earlier, addressing the meeting, MoS (EFCC), Shri Singh, suggested that a habitat-based scientific study needs to be carried out on its carrying capacity, and ascertained whether the ecosystem has sufficient resources to sustain the wildlife population. This would help in better planning of strategy to augment resources and manage human-wildlife conflict.

The meeting concluded with a detailed discussion among Members of Parliament on measures required to strengthen national and State-level efforts for reducing human–wildlife conflict while ensuring long-term conservation of India’s rich wildlife heritage.
